directions.description: For any filtered system of nilperfect rings {R_i} with colimit R, the canonical map colim ℝW(R_i) → ℝW(R) is an isomorphism of abelian groups. This conjecture addresses the fundamental motivation for sheared Witt vectors: resolving the failure of W(R)/p^n to commute with filtered colimits while preserving essential Dieudonné-theoretic properties.

directions.proof_strategy: Establish the isomorphism by proving ℝW preserves filtered colimits through the pullback definition and limit representation. Key steps: (1) Show ℎw commutes appropriately with filtered colimits using nilpotent element control, (2) Prove lim_F commutes with filtered colimits in the category of p-complete rings, (3) Apply the five lemma to the resulting diagram of short exact sequences.

directions.description:
For every simple graph G with maximum degree Δ, any number of agents ℓ ≥ 2Δ is sufficient to guarantee a stochastic‑dominance envy‑free‐up‑to‑one‑item (SD‑EF1) allocation of the vertices on the agents, and moreover there exists a deterministic polynomial‑time algorithm that produces such an allocation.  This conjecture sharpens the currently known existential and algorithmic bounds of ℓ ≥ 3Δ−1 (and ℓ ≥ (3+ε)Δ) by reducing the required number of agents to 2Δ.

In graph‑theoretic terms the conjecture asserts that every Δ‑bounded simple graph admits a proper vertex‑colouring with at most 2Δ colours in which each colour class can be mapped to an agent in such a way that the resulting allocation satisfies the SD‑EF1 condition for any common preference order.  The conjecture is falsifiable: a single counter‑example graph with Δ and ℓ < 2Δ that admits no SD‑EF1 allocation would refute it.

This conjecture is formalizable in Lean 4 as a statement about the existence of a partition of V(G) into ℓ independent sets satisfying the SD‑EF1 inequalities, coupled with an explicit algorithmic construction.

First, using a refined greedy colouring algorithm, we would show that any Δ‑bounded graph can be coloured with at most 2Δ colours while preserving an auxiliary structure that guarantees the SD‑EF1 inequalities for any common preference order.  Second, we would implement the colouring as a deterministic polynomial‑time procedure by iteratively resolving conflicts in a way that respects the strong colourability hierarchy introduced in the paper. directions.description: For an n-vertex graph that is not k-edge hamiltonian, the maximum number of t-stars is exactly g_t(n,k-1,i*) where i* = max{1, d-(k-1)} for some parameter d, and this bound is tight and achieved precisely by the graph G(n,k-1,i*) = K_{i*+k-1} + (K_{n-2i*-k+1} ∪ I_{i*})
domain_bridges: Star counting in forbidden subgraph families

directions.proof_strategy: Prove by induction on k: establish that among all non k-edge hamiltonian graphs, removing a vertex and analyzing the resulting (k-1)-edge hamiltonian subgraph leads to the recursive structure. Use discharging arguments to show that any extremal graph must have the clique-independent set structure of G(n,k-1,i*). Verify tightness by direct computation of t-star count in this construction and showing it achieves the claimed maximum.
directions.title: Extremal t-star count in non k-edge hamiltonian graphs equals G(n,k-1,i*) construction
